cli-safe-flags.name: Claude runs in CI without bypassing its permissions
cli-safe-flags.description: No Claude CLI invocation the build ran asked to skip its approval step.
cli-safe-flags.remediation:
Remove `--dangerously-skip-permissions` from the invocation, and list the tools the job actually needs instead:

```bash
claude -p --output-format json --allowedTools "Read" "Grep" "Bash(git diff:*)" 'review this diff'
```

The flag is meant for a sandbox you don't mind losing. In CI, it hands that freedom to a model reading a pull request someone outside the repository wrote, while it holds the runner's checkout, its environment and any credentials the job was given. A prompt hidden in a diff then becomes a command on the runner. `--allowedTools` gives the run what it needs and nothing more.

dangerousFlags.description: Comma separated flags that remove the approval step. Any one of them is a violation.

cli-structured-output.name: Claude answers CI in a format a program can read
cli-structured-output.description: Every headless Claude CLI invocation the build ran asked for structured output.
cli-structured-output.remediation:
Add `--output-format json` to the invocation:

```bash
claude -p --output-format json 'summarise what changed' > review.json
```

A headless run is read by a program, not a person, and reading prose means guessing: a step that greps the answer for `FAIL` passes the day the model words it differently. JSON returns the result, the cost and the session id as fields, so your job can branch on a value instead of on a phrasing.

formats.description: Comma separated `--output-format` values that count as structured.

instructions-symlinked.name: Claude reads the instruction file the repository keeps
instructions-symlinked.description: `CLAUDE.md` is a symbolic link to `AGENTS.md`, not a second copy of it or missing altogether.
instructions-symlinked.remediation:
Point the alias at the file the repository actually keeps:

```bash
ln -sf AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md
git add CLAUDE.md
```

Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, while every other agent follows the [agents.md](https://agents.md) convention and reads `AGENTS.md`. With only one of the two files, only some of the agents working in the repository get instructions. With two separate files, the instructions drift apart within a month.

Make sure the link is committed as a link. On a Windows checkout, `git config core.symlinks` must be `true`; otherwise git writes a text file containing the target's name, and that is what both agents read.

paths.description: The alias first, then the file it must be a symbolic link to. Both are relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
